correctness.rationale: Every fixed-first-one-position row contains a consecutive-pair conflict path, giving the exact upper bound by rowwise independence. The odd-gap family saturates each row; splitting pairs by parity of the first one proves common deletion descendant intersection <=1 using distinct parity patterns of the three possible weight-two descendants and the two possible weight-one descendants. All empty-prefix/suffix cases only delete candidate descendants. Exact finite checker passed through n=18; proof is all-n.

originality.rationale: The claim is the exact all-length optimal capacity of the constant-weight-two binary layer under two distinct one-deletion reads. Primary 2002 and 2012 sources concern ordinary one-read codes and weight-restricted colorings rather than this two-read independent-set number. Accessible related published reconstruction graph data count edges of an unrestricted graph, not optimal independent sets of its weight-two induced subgraphs. Foundational 2001 full text remains a caveat.
residual_risks: The full text of Levenshtein 2001 was not inspected and might contain an implied optimal fixed-weight theorem.
No exhaustive historical uniqueness search is claimed; unindexed specialist sources may cover the result.

value.rationale: An exact capacity valid for every blocklength for the natural sparse two-one source is a motivated reconstruction-coding invariant. It quantifies the benefit of two distinct deletion reads versus ordinary deletion correction and supplies an elementary explicit rate-optimal construction. Both the exact upper bound and construction are structural, not a finite table or an arbitrary slice.
